sentences.text:
This writ petition has been preferred on behalf of the Petitioners under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, seeking the following reliefs:
"a) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus thereby directing the respondents to amend their records with respect to the status of the land of the petitioners in terms of order dated 16/05/1989 passed in WP (C) 2823/1988 as well as the order dated 16/11/2005 passed in WP (C) 3160 /2000 thereby declaring that the land of the petitioners is free from acquisition under the Land Acquisition Act.
b) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus hereby directing the respondents to issue NOC to the petitioners, as the land is free from acquisition and the petitioners are entitled to deal with their land freely in terms of the Order dated 16/05/1989 passed in WP (C) 2823/1988, as they have already refunded the compensation received by them under the land acquisition act.

c) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus or Certiorari thereby directing the Respondent no. 2 & 3 to fix the responsibility of the officers who were in charge at the relevant time for amendment and upkeeping of the records, who failed to comply their duties.

Predecessors-in-interest of the Petitioners filed a writ petition being W.P.(C) No.2823/1988 titled Harbir Singh & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.', raising a grievance that despite judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in Balak Ram Gupta v. Union of India, in CWP No.1639/1985 decided on 14.10.1988 wherein proceedings under Section 5A of the 1894 Act up to the stage of Award relating to several villagers including the Village Saidulajaib were quashed, Respondents were trying to dispossess the Petitioners.

sentences.text: As proof of payment, Petitioners filed a letter dated 27.01.1994 sent by LAC to the Tehsildar, Mehrauli, communicating that the land owners including the Petitioners had refunded the compensation amount with interest in the office of the LAC and therefore, necessary amendment may be carried out in the revenue records.

Petitioners also placed on record of the Court certificates issued by the Syndicate Bank certifying that pay orders towards the compensation amount had been issued by the bank favouring LAC (M.E.), Delhi and the pay orders were collected by SBI, Tis Hazari Branch on 27.10.1993 in local clearing.

the NOC was declined by the Respondents on the frivolous ground that the land was under acquisition vide Award No. 13/87- 88 dated 20.05.1987 and Petitioners had not refunded the compensation.

Petitioners approached the Respondents and provided a copy of the judgment dated 16.05.1989 and order dated 16.11.2005 passed by this Court wherein it was recorded that compensation had been refunded and were advised to make a fresh application for grant of NOC.
Petitioners again applied on 28.12.2023 but the application was rejected on the same very ground.

This was followed by a 3rd application on 06.03.2024 but Respondents were consistent on their ground and again rejected the application, compelling the Petitioners to approach this Court.
6.

Learned counsel for the Petitioners submits that the Award No. 13/87- 88 dated 20.05.1987 in respect of their land was quashed by a Division Bench of this Court in 1988 and thereafter directions were issued to the Respondents to receive the refund of compensation by judgment dated 16.05.1989, subject to which Respondents were to amend the revenue records and ensure that possession of the Petitioners is not disturbed.

However, despite these judgments/orders,

sentences.text: 8. Heard learned counsels for the Petitioners and the Respondents.

9. Having carefully examined the rival contentions and on perusal of the documents on record and the judgments/orders of this Court in the earlier rounds of litigation between the parties, this Court finds merit in the contention of the Petitioners that the compensation amount received by them in lieu of the acquisition of their land in the aforementioned Khasra Numbers, situated in the revenue estate of Village Saidulajaib, has been refunded to the LAC, in compliance with the directions of this Court in the judgment dated 16.05.1989.

As rightly contended by the counsel for the Petitioners, this fact is completely substantiated by a letter addressed by the LAC himself on 27.01.1994 to the Tehsildar, Mehrauli intimating the receipt of compensation amount and directing the amendment of the revenue record as well as the certificates issued by the Syndicate Bank in which bank the pay orders were drawn when the refund was made and the certificates clearly reflect that the amounts mentioned in the pay orders were credited to the SBI Account of LAC maintained at Tis Hazari.
Significantly, both these facts are recorded by the Court in paragraph 8 of the judgment dated This is a digitally signed order.

"8. In proof of having returned the compensation received, writ petitioners of WP(C)
3160/2000 have filed as Annexure P.4 a communication addressed on 27.1.1994 by the LAC to the Tehsildar, Mehrauli stating that the compensation received for the lands in question by-the bhumidars has been returned together with interest.
Said document is an admitted document.

Further, the writ petitioners have filed Annexure PR-1 being certificates issued by the Syndicate Bank on which bank the pay orders were drawn when refund was made, to the effect that the amounts covered by the pay order were credited to the saving bank account maintained with the State Bank of India, Tis Hazari by the LAC.

The writ petitioners of WP(C) No.3133/2000 have likewise filed as Annexure P.1 a certificate issued by the Central Bank of India which certifies that the bankers cheque issued by the Central Bank of India have been encashed by the LAC."
10. It is an uncontroverted position that this judgment was not assailed by the Respondents and has attained finality.
